business.name: Harbor & Vine Plumbing
business.what_they_do: Residential plumbing — drain cleaning, water heaters, repiping, slab leaks, sewer camera, emergency burst pipe repair

findings.title: Phone number is not a tappable link on mobile
findings.evidence: The number “(619) 555-0142” appears as plain text; the automated check found 0 tel: links. On a phone, tapping it does nothing.
findings.confidence_reason: The check directly measured telLinks: 0 and textMatch: "(619) 555-0142". No inference needed.
findings.business_impact: Every mobile visitor who wants to call must manually copy or memorize the number. Many will abandon the effort, especially in an emergency.
findings.fix: Wrap the number in (619) 555-0142 everywhere it appears — header, body, footer.

findings.title: No viewport meta tag — mobile renders at desktop width
findings.evidence: viewportMeta is empty string; the check reports “No viewport meta tag, so phones render the page at desktop width and zoom out.”
findings.confidence_reason: Direct measurement of the missing meta tag.
findings.business_impact: The page loads tiny and zoomed out on phones. Even if the phone number were a link, users must pinch-zoom to find and tap it. Most won’t bother.
findings.fix: Add <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"> to the <head>.

findings.title: All tap targets are far below the 44 px minimum
findings.evidence: 6 of 6 visible controls under 44 px; smallest "Home" at 29×14 px.
findings.confidence_reason: Direct measurement of visible interactive elements.
findings.business_impact: Navigation links (Home, Services, About Us, Contact, Testimonials) are too small to tap reliably on a phone. Visitors cannot reach the Contact page or any other section.
findings.fix: Increase tap target size to at least 44×44 px — enlarge font, add padding, or convert to full-width mobile buttons.

findings.title: Stale "Site last updated March 2011" contradicts copyright 2024 and 35-year claim
findings.evidence: Page text reads "Site last updated March 2011" while copyright says "1998-2024" and copy claims "over thirty-five years".
findings.confidence_reason: I see the conflicting dates in the extracted page text. Only the owner can confirm whether the business is still active; the 2011 date makes the site look abandoned.
findings.business_impact: A homeowner with a burst pipe sees a site apparently untouched since 2011 and doubts the emergency number works. Trust evaporates at the moment of highest intent.
findings.fix: Remove or update the "last updated" line to today’s date. Ensure copyright year matches reality.

findings.title: Page title is only 8 characters and no meta description exists
findings.evidence: title is only 8 characters; no meta description.
findings.confidence_reason: Direct measurement of title length and missing meta description.
findings.business_impact: Search results show a generic "Plumbing" title with no descriptive snippet. Fewer searchers click through; fewer callers arrive.
findings.fix: Set a descriptive title (e.g., "Harbor & Vine Plumbing — San Diego Emergency & Residential Plumbing Since 1987") and a 150-character meta description highlighting emergency service, license, and phone number.

findings.title: 16 text elements fail WCAG AA contrast (worst 2.13:1)
findings.evidence: 16 of 56 sampled text elements below WCAG AA. Worst is 2.13:1 where 4.5:1 is required (copyright notice).
findings.confidence_reason: Direct contrast measurement against WCAG AA threshold.
findings.business_impact: Older homeowners — a core plumbing demographic — may struggle to read the phone number, hours, or address. Lost legibility = lost calls.
findings.fix: Darken the low-contrast text (especially footer copyright) against its background to meet 4.5:1.

findings.title: Heading structure broken: two H1s and skipped H2 level
findings.evidence: Heading outline is broken: 2 h1 elements; h1 is followed by h3.
findings.confidence_reason: Direct structural analysis of heading levels.
findings.business_impact: Screen readers and search crawlers misinterpret page hierarchy. Indirectly reduces discoverability and accessibility.
findings.fix: Use one H1 (business name + location), then H2 for major sections (Services, Testimonials, Contact), H3 for sub-items.

findings.title: Two images lack alt text (appear to be 1×1 tracking GIFs)
findings.evidence: 2 of 2 visible image(s) have no alt text (e.g. gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAIAAAMLCwgAAACwAAAAAAQABAAA).
findings.confidence_reason: Direct measurement of alt attribute presence.
findings.business_impact: Minor — these are likely invisible tracking pixels. No direct effect on calls, but an accessibility audit flag.
findings.fix: Add alt="" to decorative images or remove them if unused.

overall.verdict: The site has strong trust content (35 years, family-owned, licensed, testimonials) but critical mobile usability failures — no clickable phone number, no viewport tag, microscopic tap targets — that stop mobile callers cold. A stale 2011 timestamp further erodes trust at the moment of emergency. Fix the top three technical items first; they are the difference between a ringing phone and a silent one.
overall.biggest_opportunity: Add tel: links, viewport meta, and finger-sized tap targets. These three changes alone make the existing trust content reachable on mobile.
overall.redesign_brief: Lead with a prominent, tappable phone number in a sticky header on every page. Prove credibility immediately: "Licensed, bonded, insured — CA license on request", "Family-owned since 1987", "Emergency service — call (619) 555-0142". Show the two testimonials with names and dates. Cut the "Site last updated March 2011" line and the copyright mismatch. Make all navigation targets thumb-sized. Ensure the page renders at device width with a proper viewport tag.

plan.positioning: Harbor & Vine Plumbing — San Diego's family-owned emergency and residential plumber since 1987. Licensed, bonded, insured. Call (619) 555-0142.
plan.secondary_cta: None — phone call is the only conversion goal

sections.name: Sticky Header
sections.purpose: Answer f1 (phone not tappable), f3 (tap targets too small), f6 (contrast). Make the phone number reachable on every scroll position.
sections.content_notes: Full-width bar, high-contrast background (dark navy #1B2A4A) with white text. Single element: the phone number as a tel: link, minimum 48px tap height, 18px font, generous padding. Text: 'Call (619) 555-0142 — Emergency Service'. No navigation links, no logo, no hamburger menu. The header *is* the CTA.

sections.name: Hero / Above Fold
sections.purpose: Answer f4 (stale 2011 timestamp destroys trust), f5 (weak title/meta), f7 (broken heading hierarchy). Establish credibility in the first 3 seconds.
sections.content_notes: Single H1: 'Harbor & Vine Plumbing — San Diego Emergency & Residential Plumbing Since 1987'. Sub-headline (not a heading): 'Family-owned, second generation. Fully licensed, bonded & insured. CA license on request. Call (619) 555-0142.' No hero image. No slogan. The proof statements are the design.

sections.name: Services
sections.purpose: Answer f7 (H2 for major section). Close the sale by showing exactly what the business does — matches search intent.
sections.content_notes: H2: 'Residential Plumbing Services'. Unstyled list, each line a service from verified context: Drain cleaning and hydro jetting; Water heater repair and replacement; Repiping (copper and PEX); Slab leak detection; Sewer camera inspection; Emergency burst pipe repair. No icons, no cards, no 'learn more' links. Just the services.

sections.name: Proof & Credentials
sections.purpose: Answer f4 (trust), f7 (H2). Convert credibility claims into scannable facts.
sections.content_notes: H2: 'Licensed, Bonded, Insured'. Three bullet lines: 'California contractor license — available on request'; 'Fully bonded and insured for your protection'; 'Family-owned and operated since 1987 — Ray Vine, second generation owner'. No badges, no certificate images, no third-party seals.

sections.name: Testimonials
sections.purpose: Answer f4 (trust), f7 (H2). Real words from real customers — the audit notes two exist.
sections.content_notes: H2: 'What San Diego Homeowners Say'. Two blockquotes, each with name and date (from existing site content). No star ratings, no carousel, no 'read more'. If the existing testimonials have no dates, use 'Verified customer' and omit date rather than fabricate.

sections.name: Service Area
sections.purpose: Close the sale by confirming the caller is in the right place.
sections.content_notes: H2: 'We Serve San Diego'. One sentence: 'Harbor & Vine Plumbing serves all of San Diego — coastal, inland, and surrounding neighborhoods.' No map, no zip code list, no 'check availability' tool.

sections.name: Footer CTA
sections.purpose: Answer f1 (phone tappable), f3 (tap target size), f6 (contrast), f7 (heading hierarchy). Final chance to call.
sections.content_notes: H2: 'Emergency or Routine — Call Now'. Tel: link again, same 48px minimum tap height, high contrast. Text: 'Call (619) 555-0142'. Copyright line: '© 1987–2025 Harbor & Vine Plumbing. All rights reserved.' No 'site last updated' line. No email, no contact form, no social links.

must_not_claim: Specific California license number (context says 'on request')
Number of employees or crew size
plan.design_direction: Mobile-first, single column, no breakpoints needed — the page *is* the mobile view. Dark navy (#1B2A4A) and white for header/footer; black text on off-white (#FAFAF9) for body. System font stack (San Francisco / Segoe UI / Roboto). No gradients, no shadows, no animations, no illustrations. Tap targets minimum 48×48px. Contrast minimum 7:1 for phone number, 4.5:1 for all body text. Page weight target < 100KB HTML+CSS. No JavaScript required. Viewport meta tag present. One H1, three H2s, no skipped levels. Decorative images (if any) get alt="".

Your phone number isn’t a tappable link on mobile, and the page has no viewport meta tag, so phones render it at desktop width and the contact button is too small to tap reliably.

It costs $1,800 USD for a rebuilt, mobile‑first single‑page site that passes all the checks I run.

the rebuilt page - I rebuilt your page so you can look at it instead of imagining it: http://localhost:3000/mockup/demo-harbor-vine-plumbing-example

That page is a concept mockup I made, not affiliated with Harbor & Vine Plumbing. It passed 11 of 13 automated checks, against 3 of 13 for the current page.

Take a look at the page I built and reply yes or no.
